summary: Michael Atkins, a 40-year-old architect with two decades in construction, pivots into tech, challenging the stereotype that technology belongs to the young. He started with an online coding course, endured rejections, leaned on mentorship and community, and used his architecture and project skills to land a role at a smart city start-up in January 2024. His story argues that learning is lifelong and that diverse experience is an asset.
one_line: At 40, architect Michael Atkins leaves construction for tech, landing a smart city start-up job by leveraging his experience, mentors, and persistence.
key_facts: Michael Atkins was 40 years old when he began his move into tech, with the story marking September 14, 2023 as the start of his challenge to age stereotypes.
Michael Atkins worked for two decades as an architect, with a career of hard hats, blueprints and construction sites rather than software boot camps or computer science degrees.
In October 2023, while inspecting a historic building renovation, Michael realized that if old walls could adapt to modern needs, so could he.
Michael enrolled in an online coding course while still overseeing construction projects, often working sleepless nights.
Michael applied for internships and junior developer positions and faced a stack of rejections, which at first felt like confirmation that he was too old.
Michael's architecture background, ability to visualize projects and manage complex builds translated into project management in software teams and tech-led construction firms.
Michael also explored 3D modelling and BIM (Building Information Modeling) as emerging tech sectors matching his skills.
Michael attended meetups, engaged in coding forums, and connected with other career-switchers to find his 'tribe'.
On November 20, 2023, at a tech networking event, Michael met Linda Shah, a software engineer who became an essential guide and friend.
In late January 2024, on a Tuesday afternoon, a tech start-up specializing in smart city solutions responded to Michael's application, seeking someone with construction background and tech interest.
Michael underwent rigorous training to catch up on tech and smart city innovation, describing the learning curve as steep.
Michael says his story is about building connections, both the physical ones he made as an architect and the intangible ties to people and new experiences.
